source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Collect all fire inspection records, both digital and hard copies, that are related to the building in question. This includes initial inspections, re-inspections, and any follow-up assessments. Ensure these records are up-to-date and reflect the most recent conditions.

3. Review the failed items.
Go through the inspection reports and list all fire safety items that have been marked as "failed" or "not compliant." These may include malfunctioning fire alarms, malfunctioning sprinklers, blocked emergency exits, accumulation of hazardous materials, improper storage of flammable substances, lack of emergency lights, and outdated firefighting equipment.

4. Photograph failed items.
Take clear, well-documented photos of all failed items identified during the inspection. Date and time-stamp the images and label each photo to correspond with the item on your list. Make sure these images clearly show the reasons for the failure, such as severance in sprinkler pipes, broken emergency lights, or blocked evacuation routes
